n:UBS: UBS is a bank based in Zurich, Switzerland. Axel Weber, president of Germany's Deutsche Bundesbank until April 2011, went from that post to chairman of UBS, and Joseph Yam, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority from 1 April 1993 to 30 September 2009, later sat on the board of UBS AG / UBS Group AG and was an independent non-executive director of China Construction Bank. Gail Kelly, a member of its board of directors, represents UBS in the Group of Thirty, a forum where central bankers also sit. UBS is one of the firms named in Janet Yellen's financial disclosures, reported in January 2021, which show the former Federal Reserve chair made more than 7 million US dollars from speeches in recent years, including 952,200 dollars from Citigroup. It also keeps gold for the Bank of Ghana: a report of 30 September 2021, drawing on the bank's 2020 annual report, puts about 907 million Ghana cedis of gold reserves with UBS, which is custody of a reserve asset rather than managing the money. These are jobs and business ties, not accusations.
n:Standard Chartered: Standard Chartered is a bank based in London, United Kingdom. Sheila M'mbijjewe was a director of Standard Chartered Bank, a non-executive director of Ecobank and a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers before becoming Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya. Maria Ramos represents the bank in the Group of Thirty, a forum where central bankers also sit; the G30 listing gives her as Chair, and her biography says she has been Senior Independent Director since 2022. Standard Chartered is also among the firms named in Janet Yellen's financial disclosures, reported in January 2021, as paying the former Federal Reserve chair for speeches. It holds gold for Bangladesh Bank: reporting of 8 September 2026 said that as of June it held 92,739 troy ounces, worth around 45.66 billion taka, in the United Kingdom, custody of a reserve asset rather than managing the money.
n:JPMorgan Chase: JPMorgan Chase is a bank with its parent in New York, United States. It is the largest shareholder of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, with 60,600,000 shares, or 29.5 per cent, as at 31 December 2018, down from 41.7 per cent in 2007, according to a 24 February 2020 article in Institutional Investor based on a freedom-of-information release of the New York Fed's capital stock records. At the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors; since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. Several central bankers have worked at the bank. Jacob Frenkel, a former Governor of the Bank of Israel, was chairman of JPMorgan Chase International, with no dates or order given. J. Aloysius Tarlue, Jr. was a compliance officer at J.P. Morgan Chase before becoming Executive Governor of the Central Bank of Liberia in 2020. Luis Caputo came from trading and country-head roles at JP Morgan and Deutsche Bank to head Argentina's central bank from June to 25 September 2018. Yaseen Anwar trained at JPMorgan Chase from 1973 to 1975 before a career that led to Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2007 and Governor in October 2011. Lim Ji-won worked at JP Morgan's Seoul branch from 1999 to 2018 and then joined the Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Committee on 17 May 2018. The bank also holds gold for the Bank of Mongolia: its 2021 audited accounts say monetary gold and silver are mainly placed at the Bank of England and JP Morgan Chase Bank, against gold bullion of 1,594,121 million tugrik at 31 December 2021. These are jobs and business ties, not accusations.
n:ING: ING is a bank based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Robert P. Forrestal was president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta from 7 December 1983 until 1 January 1996, and after retiring he sat on the board of ING North America and on the ING Advisory Council in the Netherlands; no ethics finding is recorded, and he died in 2004. Valeria Gontareva came from Societe Generale, ING Bank and Investment Capital Ukraine to be Governor of the National Bank of Ukraine from 2014 to 2017, and Thomas Domhoff came from project roles at ING, ABN AMRO, Rabobank and Capgemini, and a directorship at Banco Sicredi, to be President of the Central Bank of Aruba from 1 July 2026. ING is also among the firms named in Janet Yellen's financial disclosures, reported in January 2021, as paying the former Federal Reserve chair for speeches. These are jobs, not accusations.
n:Absa Group: Absa Group is a bank in Johannesburg, South Africa. It holds 10,000 shares in the South African Reserve Bank, about 0.5 per cent of the bank's 2 million shares and the most any one holder may own, according to a news report of 25 August 2023 citing the Reserve Bank's shareholder index as at 30 June 2022; the Reserve Bank's own site confirms the share total and the cap but names no holders. In June 2017 the Public Protector ordered Absa to repay 1.125 billion rand for an apartheid-era Reserve Bank rescue loan to Bankorp. On 16 February 2018 the Pretoria High Court set that report and its remedial action aside on review applications by the Reserve Bank and Absa, and ordered the Public Protector to pay part of the Reserve Bank's costs personally. Gill Marcus went from chairwoman of Absa Group to Governor of the South African Reserve Bank from 9 November 2009, having been deputy governor from 1999 to 2004.
n:AKO Capital: AKO Capital is a hedge fund firm based in London, United Kingdom, whose founder Nicolai Tangen was appointed on 24 March 2020 as chief executive of Norges Bank Investment Management, the arm of Norway's central bank that runs the country's oil fund. In 2020 Norges Bank's Supervisory Council warned that the hire could carry a risk of breaking laws, rules and guidelines, said Tangen still appeared to be AKO Capital's main owner with voting control despite the bank saying he had cut those ties, and said the bank had not handled transparency about the applicant list as expected. In August 2020 the bank's Executive Board changed his employment terms to answer conflict-of-interest concerns raised by the Storting's Standing Committee on Finance and Economic Affairs: he would sell his holding in AKO Capital LLP and transfer his holding and dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation, with no ownership interest in AKO Capital in perpetuity, and would hold all his personal fund assets as bank deposits. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said there had been a breach of guidelines, regulations and laws in the appointment; Executive Board chair Oystein Olsen said the board had thought the existing contract was enough but accepted that the Storting took a different view. Tangen was able to take office on 1 September.
n:AIA Group: AIA Group is an insurance group based in Hong Kong. Ong Chong Tee, previously Deputy Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, is listed as a director of AIA Group; he also joined the board of United Overseas Bank on 1 January 2023, chairs its audit committee, and is chairman of the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority. No ethics finding is recorded. Tan Sri Mohamed Azman Yahya was an independent non-executive director of AIA Group Limited from 24 February 2014 to 28 May 2020 and joined Bank Negara Malaysia's board of directors four days later, on 1 June 2020. These are career moves, not accusations.
n:Bear Stearns: Bear Stearns is a bank in New York, United States, and two Federal Reserve officials worked there. Wayne D. Angell came from officer and director roles at banks in Kansas and Missouri to a seat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, sworn in on 7 February 1986 and retiring on 2 February 1994, and on leaving became chief economist at Bear Stearns & Co., Inc.; no ethics finding is recorded. Lawrence K. Roos came from the First National Bank of St. Louis to the presidency of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which he held from 1976 to 1983, and then went on to Bear, Stearns and Company.
n:Northern Trust: Northern Trust is a bank and asset servicing firm based in Chicago, United States. Its 2025 annual report shows an average holding of 70 million US dollars of Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago stock; at the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors, and since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. J. Charles Partee came from the Northern Trust Company of Chicago to the Federal Reserve's staff and then a governorship from 5 January 1976 to 7 February 1986, and afterwards joined the board of State Farm Insurance and a mutual fund trusteeship. For the Bank of Botswana, Central Banking's global custodian award profile says Northern Trust provides performance measurement and attribution reporting and runs training for bank staff on benchmark construction and fixed-income investment. For the Bank of Uganda it provides compliance, performance and risk sensitivity analysis, helped build a dashboard for overseeing the bank's external asset managers alongside monthly audited reports, and supported a redesign of the bank's strategic asset allocation system. In both cases the profile describes services, training and advice rather than managing the money.
n:State Tribunal of Poland: The State Tribunal is the court in Warsaw that tries senior Polish officials for breaking the law in office. In March 2024 members of parliament from the ruling coalition filed a motion to bring Adam Glapinski, president of the National Bank of Poland, before it on eight charges, among them bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and unauthorised currency interventions. The motion, begun in May 2024, accuses him of indirectly financing the deficit through asset purchases in 2020 and 2021 and of acting without proper authorisation from the Monetary Policy Council for those purchases and for foreign-exchange interventions. Glapinski and the bank called the allegations baseless, and no vote had taken place. Nothing has been proven.
n:Directorate of Public Prosecutions of: The Directorate of Public Prosecutions, in Gaborone, brings criminal cases on behalf of the state in Botswana. Headed by Stephen Tiroyakgosi, it called in Moses Pelaelo, Governor of the Bank of Botswana, to hear his account of 100 billion pula that the state alleged had been looted from the central bank by former president Ian Khama and former intelligence chief Isaac Kgosi. Tiroyakgosi said Pelaelo told them no money is missing from the Bank of Botswana, and that the investigation was continuing; the allegations are unproven. In the same affair a woman arrested on 17 October 2019 had been implicated with Khama, Kgosi and others in allegedly stealing 100 billion pula from the Bank of Botswana. High Court Judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and of a false passport declaration, the state withdrew a terrorism financing charge, and he found the accusations fabricated and referred the investigator to police for prosecution for perjury.
n:PwC: PwC is an accounting firm based in London, United Kingdom, and it audits the accounts of ten central banks and of the Bank for International Settlements, the bank for central banks. Its Finnish arm was recommended as auditor of the Bank of Finland on 7 October 2025 and approved by a Council decision of 13 November 2025 for the financial years 2026 to 2031, and its Portuguese arm was approved by a Council decision of 12 July 2022 for the Bank of Portugal for 2022 to 2026. At the Bank of Canada it audits jointly with Ernst & Young, with a report dated 26 February 2026 on the 2025 accounts. It signed the 2025 accounts of the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (report dated 30 April 2026), Danmarks Nationalbank (Copenhagen, 24 February 2026), the Central Bank of Brazil and the National Bank of Kazakhstan, the South African Reserve Bank's accounts for the year ended 31 March 2023 (report of 12 June 2023), and the Saudi Central Bank's for the fiscal year ended 30 June 2023. For the Bank for International Settlements it audited the year to 31 March 2026, the seventh and final year of its term, with a new auditor to be proposed. Sheila M'mbijjewe was a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers, as well as a director of Standard Chartered Bank and a non-executive director of Ecobank, before becoming Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya. The firm also appears in one case: a July 2013 report by the UN Monitoring Group for Somalia and Eritrea said 80 per cent of withdrawals from the Central Bank of Somalia were made for private purposes and that the governor was key to irregularities, with 12 million of 16.9 million US dollars transferred by PricewaterhouseCoopers untraceable. The central bank rejected the allegations.
n:Cristina Fernández de Kirchner: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner is a former president of Argentina, based in Buenos Aires. Her government called on Martin Redrado, head of the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic, to resign on 6 January, saying he refused to back its decree calling for 6.6 billion US dollars of reserves; he refused to go, and on 7 January she issued a second decree firing him and accusing him of misconduct. On 8 January the courts suspended both decrees. Redrado resigned later that month; a page dated 30 January 2010 reports that an Argentine court held that she needed the approval of the full Congress to use the bank's reserves, and that the reserves stayed frozen while lawmakers were expected to take the matter up in March. She was later tried, with Vanoli, Pesce, former economy minister Kicillof and others, for defrauding the state through the central bank's sales of dollar futures between August and November 2015. On 13 April 2021 the Federal Court of Criminal Cassation unanimously dismissed the case against all fifteen defendants.
n:Government of Argentina: The Government of Argentina, based in Buenos Aires, has two recorded dealings with the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic. Under President Néstor Kirchner it was to replace the central bank's president, Alfonso Prat-Gay, whose term ended that week, with Martin Redrado, subject to Senate approval; the report says the trigger was unclear, local media suggested disagreements over the debt restructuring, and neither side is quoted. In May 2023, an election year, the central bank transferred a further 140 billion Argentine pesos to the Treasury as temporary advances, bringing transfers since March to 370 billion pesos and using 99.2 per cent of the 372.8 billion peso first-half limit agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
n:Council of Representatives of Iraq: The Council of Representatives is Iraq's parliament, based in Baghdad. Sinan Al Shabibi, governor of the Central Bank of Iraq, was removed and a successor named during a parliamentary probe into possible manipulation of the dinar against the dollar. A committee member said arrest warrants had been issued for 30 people, including Al Shabibi and his deputy, Mudher Saleh. The integrity committee chairman said the probe was "not about money, but about procedures", while a finance committee member called it "a political decision and not professional", and no statement from Al Shabibi is reported. In October 2012 Iraq's cabinet removed him after a parliamentary committee charged that bank officials were abusing the central bank's dollar sales, and the Supreme Judicial Council confirmed arrest warrants for him and other officials without giving the charges. His defence called the case politically motivated, and the accusations are unproven.
n:Board of Supreme Audit (Iraq): This is Iraq's state audit agency, in Baghdad. Under Coalition Provisional Authority Order Number 56, the central bank law of 2004, it audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Iraq. In 2012 it investigated the central bank's daily dollar auctions and found that most transactions were based on fraudulent paperwork, and according to the US Special Inspector General for Iraq Reconstruction its top auditor told US officials that up to 800 million US dollars a week was leaving Iraq illegally.
n:Austrian Mint: The Austrian Mint, or Münze Österreich AG, is a company in Vienna and a subsidiary of the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, Austria's central bank. The Nationalbank says 50 tons of its gold sit in the Mint's vaults, part of the 140 tons it keeps inside Austria out of 280 tons in total. The Mint is also named in a case against former managers of OeBS, the Nationalbank's banknote printing subsidiary, who were tried for paying kickbacks to the central banks of Azerbaijan, through a 20 per cent overcharge, and Syria, through 14 per cent, to win banknote orders, with about 14 million euros paid. Seven defendants were convicted in October 2014; after a retrial ordered by the Supreme Court, the Vienna court in February 2018 gave Wolf and Miller 18-month suspended terms and Meyer 21 months suspended, and acquitted former Nationalbank deputy governor Duchatczek. Being named in the case is not a finding against the Mint.
n:Goldman Sachs: Goldman Sachs is a bank based in New York, United States. It holds 8,300,000 shares, or 4 per cent, of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York as at 31 December 2018, according to a 24 February 2020 article in Institutional Investor based on a freedom-of-information release of the New York Fed's capital stock records; at the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors, and since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. Many central bankers have worked there. Mario Draghi was vice chairman and managing director of Goldman Sachs International from 2002 to 2005 before becoming governor of the Bank of Italy and later European Central Bank president, and Otmar Issing went the other way, from ECB chief economist to international adviser at Goldman Sachs. Hafize Gaye Erkan came from Goldman Sachs managing director and co-chief executive of First Republic Bank to governor of the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye from June 2023. Mark Carney spent thirteen years at the bank before becoming Governor of the Bank of Canada from 1 February 2008 to 1 June 2013. At the Federal Reserve, William Dudley came from partner, managing director and chief US economist at Goldman Sachs to the New York Fed in 2007; Neel Kashkari, Beth M. Hammack and Robert S. Kaplan came from the firm to the Minneapolis, Cleveland and Dallas Reserve Banks; and E. Gerald Corrigan went from president of the New York Fed, which he led from 1 January 1985 to 19 July 1993, to partner at Goldman Sachs. At the Bank of England, Huw Pill came from chief European economist and Ben Broadbent from senior European economist at the firm to the Monetary Policy Committee, Broadbent later becoming Deputy Governor for Monetary Policy. Tito Mboweni, governor of the South African Reserve Bank for a decade until 2009, became an international adviser to Goldman Sachs in 2010 and returned as a regional adviser in an appointment announced in February 2022. Greg Swart, a director on the board of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, spent about twelve years at Goldman Sachs before Farallon Capital Management. Goldman Sachs is also among the firms named in Janet Yellen's financial disclosures, reported in January 2021, as paying the former Federal Reserve chair for speeches; she pledged to seek written authorization before taking part in matters related to Goldman Sachs and several other firms.
n:Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley is a bank based in New York, United States. Two of its entities together hold 3.7 per cent of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, 4,800,000 shares and 2,800,000 shares as at 31 December 2018, according to a 24 February 2020 article in Institutional Investor based on a freedom-of-information release of the New York Fed's capital stock records; at the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors, and since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. Several officials have moved between the firm and central banks. Kevin Warsh went from Morgan Stanley mergers and acquisitions, as vice president and executive director, through the White House to a Federal Reserve governorship. Thomas C. Melzer came from managing director at Morgan Stanley to president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which he led from 1 June 1985 to 30 January 1998, and Alfred Hayes, president of the New York Fed from 1956 to 1975, went from there to Morgan Stanley International as chairman. At the Bank of England, David Miles came from chief UK economist at the firm and Kristin Forbes from Morgan Stanley, before an academic post at MIT, to the Monetary Policy Committee. Fahad Al-Mubarak came from chairman and managing director of Morgan Stanley Saudi Arabia to governor of the Saudi Central Bank from 2011 to 2016 and again from January 2021. Oleg Vyugin, a First Deputy Chairman of the Bank of Russia, also held private finance roles at Troika Dialog, Morgan Stanley Bank, MDM Bank and Binbank, with no dates given. These are jobs and shareholdings, not accusations.
n:Sejm of Poland: The Sejm is the lower house of Poland's parliament, in Warsaw, and it is handling the case against Adam Glapiński, president of the National Bank of Poland. Ruling coalition members of parliament filed a motion in March 2024 to send him to the State Tribunal, the court that tries senior officials, with eight accusations, among them bond purchases in 2020 and 2021 said to have indirectly financed the deficit by at least 144 billion zloty, and breaching the bank's political neutrality. The motion, begun in May 2024, also accuses him of acting without proper authorisation from the Monetary Policy Council for those purchases and for foreign-exchange interventions. The Constitutional Tribunal ruled on 12 January 2024 that a three-fifths majority was needed rather than a simple majority, against a coalition holding 241 of 460 seats where the threshold was 276, and on 20 August 2024, in a five-judge panel including chief justice Julia Przylebska, it ruled that the law allowing him to be brought before the constitutional accountability committee is unconstitutional. A committee adopted its report on 9 October 2026 and the Sejm must still decide; no vote had taken place. Glapiński and the bank call the accusations entirely groundless, and nothing has been proven.
n:Attorney General's Office (Libya): The Attorney General's Office of Libya appears in two matters involving the Central Bank of Libya. It reported in October 2023 that the Misrata Criminal Court had convicted two people of belonging to an organization set up to seize 128 million US dollars and 5 million euros from the central bank's Sirte branch in 2013 through coercion; one was given 15 years in prison and a fine of 2.5 million Libyan dinars, the other 13 years and a fine of 50,000 dinars. In November 2022 the central bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar banknotes it said were printed in Russia and bore his signature, and Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint. The bank did not say how many notes were involved, no response from al-Hibri is reported, and the accusation is unproven.
n:Assembleia da República committee of i: This was a committee of inquiry set up by Portugal's parliament, the Assembleia da República in Lisbon, to examine losses at the bank Novo Banco. On 20 July 2021 its rapporteur, Fernando Anastácio, presented a proposed final report saying supervision had failed across the board and that there was a permanent and systematic failure; that was a draft, and the PSD said its deputies would vote against it and propose amendments. On Tuesday 27 July 2021 the committee approved its final report, with the PS voting against and the CDS-PP abstaining. The report concludes that the winding up of Banco Espírito Santo and the initial capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, and it leaves criticism of the Bank of Portugal and the European Commission; the criticisms are not set out and no Bank of Portugal officials are named.
n:Supreme Court of Thailand: The Supreme Court of Thailand, in Bangkok, appears in two matters involving the Bank of Thailand. A case was brought in 2001 after former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, among other policy-makers, decided to use the central bank's reserves to defend the baht during the Asian financial crisis; on 5 October 2016 the Supreme Court upheld a lower court's ruling that he had not acted improperly, closing the 15-year case and clearing him. Its Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions also convicted former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee of malfeasance under Section 157 of the Criminal Code for appointing Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi in 2008 to the committee that selects Bank of Thailand board members, all three being representatives of financial institutions under the bank's supervision. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and a fine of 20,000 baht. The National Anti-Corruption Commission had filed the case on 27 May 2015.
